# `board_only_shared_reference.ipc.bin`

A single `kiapi.board.types.FootprintInstance`, serialised exactly as KiCad's
IPC API sent it, for a **board-only footprint carrying the reference `REF**`** —
one of two such footprints on the same board.

Decoded by `pcb_sync`'s regression tests for issue #452, where the remaining
defect was `duplicate_board_reference` refusing to sync a board whose
unannotated graphics all share KiCad's default reference. The sibling capture
[`board_only_footprint.ipc.bin`](board_only_footprint.ipc.README.md) cannot
witness that case: its mounting hole is annotated `MH1`.

## Provenance

| | |
|---|---|
| KiCad | 10.0.6, macOS (Apple Silicon) |
| Source board | `crates/konnect-ipc/tests/fixtures/board_only_shared_reference.kicad_pcb` |
| Item | one of the board's two `MountingHole:MountingHole_2.7mm_M2.5_DIN965` instances, neither of which carries a `(path ...)` line and both of which are named `REF**` |
| Transport | `GetItems` over the running editor's IPC socket |
| Captured | 2026-09-09 |
| Size | 2063 bytes |

The source board was written by KiCad itself, through the PCB editor's own
scripting API: `NewBoard`, then `FootprintLoad` against the stock
`MountingHole.pretty` twice, then `SaveBoard`. Nothing about it is
hand-authored — KiCad's parser read its own `.kicad_mod`, KiCad's writer wrote
the board, and `REF**` is the reference string that library file already
carries. That is also the point the fixture exists to record: a board can hold
two board-only footprints with the same reference without anything being wrong
with it, because the library's own default is what put it there.

It is a new board rather than two more footprints on `live_ipc.kicad_pcb`,
which is deliberately still in the legacy KiCad 9 format (`version 20241229`,
against this board's `20260206`). Saving that fixture from KiCad 10 upgrades it
in place and destroys the legacy-format coverage it exists to provide.

## Regenerating it

Set `KONNECT_CAPTURE_IPC_FIXTURE=1` when running the ignored live test
`kicad_reports_the_same_reference_for_two_board_only_footprints` in
`crates/konnect-ipc/tests/live_kicad_test.rs`. That test also *verifies* the
properties this capture exists to encode — that the shared reference is
`REF**`, that IPC returns as many footprints under it as the file carries, and
that each arrives with a present-but-empty `SheetPath` — so a regeneration that
changes the answer fails rather than silently rewriting the fixture.

The live test needs a running KiCad with its API enabled, a **copy** of the
board above open, and `KICAD_API_SOCKET` pointing at the PCB editor's socket.
Resolve that by matching `api-<pid>.sock` to a live `pcbnew` process: a stale
socket from a closed session can be newer by mtime than the live one.

`the_shared_reference_fixture_still_carries_a_duplicate_board_only_reference`
checks the board's side of this without KiCad and is **not** `#[ignore]`d, so CI
runs it. It is what lets the unit tests build their duplicate pair by varying
only the KIID: that the board really carries two `REF**` footprints is checked,
not assumed.

## The KIID variation, stated plainly

`pcb_sync`'s tests decode this one message twice and give the second copy a
different KIID, because the planner keys on KIID and a board needs two distinct
objects. **Nothing else is varied — in particular not the reference**, which is
the shared value the tests are about and is exactly what KiCad sent.

An undocumented variation is a hand-built fixture wearing a capture's name, so:
one field, named here and in the helper's doc comment, backed by the guard test
above.

## Redaction

Nothing was removed. The message was checked for filesystem paths, usernames,
hostnames and the board filename before being committed; it contains only
KiCad's stock `MountingHole` library strings, standard field names, protobuf
type URLs and KIIDs generated by KiCad for this board. `symbol_sheet_name` and
`symbol_sheet_filename` — the two fields that could carry a path — are empty
strings on a board-only footprint, which is why there is nothing to redact.

## On `ki_fp_filters`, which a reviewer will ask about

CONTRIBUTING requires real-KiCad fixtures and names a specific failure: a
hand-written footprint missing `(property ki_fp_filters "…")`. The source board
here has none — and neither does `live_ipc.kicad_pcb`, the board upstream ships
and the source of the capture accepted in #504.

Across the tracked `.kicad_pcb` fixtures, `ki_fp_filters` appears **only on
boards whose footprints carry `(path ...)`** — `pic_programmer` (49),
`ecc83-pp` (6), `RoyalBlue54L-NFC-Antenna` (1). Every board with no pathed
footprint has zero, this one and `live_ipc.kicad_pcb` included. The property
comes from the schematic symbol a footprint was placed for, so its absence on a
board-only mounting hole is correct rather than a sign of a synthetic file.
